modes.title: Two ways to run
modes.subtitle: The same TypeScript can be interpreted on the spot or compiled ahead-of-time to a .NET assembly. You choose per command.

interpret.title: Interpret
interpret.desc: Tree-walking execution with instant startup and no build step — ideal for scripting, the REPL, and rapid iteration. Just point SharpTS at a file.

compile.title: Compile (AOT)
compile.desc: Emit a real .NET assembly that runs natively on the CLR. The same path can also produce a self-contained executable, a NuGet package (--pack), or a reference assembly for C# interop (--ref-asm).

typing.title: Typed first, then run
typing.subtitle: SharpTS type-checks your whole program before it runs — then the types step aside and only the values matter.

compileTime.title: Compile time — types
compileTime.desc: The type checker validates every expression against TypeScript's rules: nominal typing for classes, structural typing for interfaces. A type error stops the program before it runs.

runtime.title: Runtime — values
runtime.desc: Once the checks pass, the types drop away and your program runs on plain values — just like compiled JavaScript. The safety you get while writing costs nothing while running.

typing.caption: Structural typing in action: Dog satisfies Walkable simply because it has a walk() method — no explicit "implements" required.

dotnet.title: TypeScript that runs on .NET
dotnet.subtitle: Because SharpTS targets the CLR, your TypeScript becomes a first-class .NET citizen — calling into .NET and callable from it.

cap1.title: Call .NET from TypeScript
cap1.body: Reach into the BCL with the @DotNetType decorator — StringBuilder, Guid, DateTime, TimeSpan — with automatic conversion and overload resolution.

cap2.title: Consume TypeScript from C#
cap2.body: Compile with --ref-asm to get a reference assembly, then instantiate your TypeScript classes and call their methods directly from C#, fully typed.

cap3.title: Ship real .NET artifacts
cap3.body: Produce a .NET assembly, a self-contained executable, or a versioned NuGet package straight from your TypeScript source.

cap4.title: MSBuild SDK
cap4.body: Add SharpTS.Sdk to a project file and build .ts files as part of your normal .NET build, driven by tsconfig.json.

cap5.title: Editor tooling from the compiler itself
cap5.body: An LSP bridge exposes SharpTS' own type checker to VS Code through the vscode-sharpts extension, so the editor and the runtime can't disagree. Declaration generation goes the other way, turning .NET types into .d.ts files — the interop surface is typed too.

architecture.title: How It Works
architecture.subtitle: A multi-stage pipeline from source to execution
architecture.selectHint: Select a stage above to see what it does.

explain.lexer: A single-pass scan turns the raw TypeScript source into a stream of tokens — keywords, identifiers, literals, and operators — the vocabulary the parser reads.
explain.parser: A recursive-descent parser reads the tokens and builds an Abstract Syntax Tree of immutable records, desugaring constructs like for-loops into while-loops and expanding destructuring along the way.
explain.typeChecker: Statically validates the AST against TypeScript's type rules before anything runs — nominal typing for classes, structural typing for interfaces. Type errors stop the program here.
explain.interpreter: Tree-walks the validated AST and executes it directly, with no build step — the fast path behind the REPL and the playground. Runtime values live in their own environment, separate from the types.
explain.ilCompiler: The ahead-of-time path: lowers the program to .NET IL across roughly twenty phases — closures become display classes, async and generators become state machines — and emits a real .NET assembly.
